newsitem.title: USA: Nordstrom says holiday sales moderately lower.
newsitem.headline: Nordstrom says holiday sales moderately lower.

text.p: Upscale retailer Nordstrom Inc. said Friday that holiday season sales in stores open for more than one year declined moderately from last year.
The Seattle-based company said the lower sales volume will result in earnings for the quarter ending Jan. 31 being below those currently expected by analysts.

According to First Call, analysts had been forecasting Nordstrom to report fourth quarter earnings of 80 cents a share vs. 67 cents a year ago. In last year's fourth quarter, Nordstrom earned $54 million on revenues of $1.2 billion.
John Goesling, Nordstrom executive vice president, said "the decline is attributable in part to fewer shopping days between Thanksgiving and Christmas."
The announcement came after the close of trading. Nordstrom stock, which had fallen 50 cents to $37.50, dropped $2.50 to $35 in after-hours trading.
